programme.title: Tuesday Documentary
programme.desc: In just four months, the world's first jumbo jet goes into regular service over the Atlantic. Already 200 have been ordered by the world's airlines. Each is designed to carry nearly 500 passengers. The jumbo has been called a 'pilot's dream.' But will it also be an airport's nightmare?By next year, half a dozen of the giants may be queuing at peak hours to disgorge their passengers at London Airport. Round the world, airports face their biggest jam in history.

programme.title: All About the Good Life
programme.desc: What was it really like behind-the-scenes of `The Good Life'? With contributions from Richard Briers, Penelope Keith, Monty Don, Brian Sewell and John O'Farrell amongst others, `All About the Good Life' explores the enduring appeal of one of the nation's best loved sitcoms.

programme.title: Frozen Planet II
programme.desc: Mountains create frozen habitats on every continent on Earth, and each of these high-altitude worlds holds unique challenges for its surprising and remarkable life. The journey begins close to the equator, the furthest point from the poles, in East Africa. Here on the high slopes of Mount Kenya, during the day the tropical sun keeps the cold at bay, but at night the frost descends.

programme.title: Frozen Planet II
programme.desc: Antarctica is the most hostile of all Earth's frozen worlds. Yet even here, amongst some of the most challenging conditions on the planet, life finds a way not just to survive, but thrive. The journey begins at the far edge of the continent, on its far-flung sub-Antarctic islands. Here there are king penguins that, to feed at sea, must face the danger of ferocious leopard seals lurking in the shallows.

programme.title: Shackleton's Cabin
programme.desc: Conservator Sven Habermann sets out to bring Earnest Shackleton's cabin, dating from his final Antarctic expedition on board the Quest, back to its original state after a twist of fate brought the artefact to Letterfrack.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Why has Antarctica, the most inhospitable place on the planet, exerted such a powerful hold on the imagination of explorers, scientists, writers and photographers. From the logbooks of Captain Cook to the diaries of Scott and Shackleton, from the Rime of the Ancient Mariner to HP Lovecraft, it's a film about real and imaginary tales of adventure, romance and tragedy.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: It's spring for the mountain goats of Glacier National Park in Canada's Rocky Mountains. The young goats will have to learn how to survive in this beautiful but treacherous wilderness.

programme.title: Tony Marchant Remembers...Take Me Home
programme.desc: Writer Tony Marchant looks back on his 1989 drama `Take Me Home', a troubled love story set amidst a political backdrop of changing attitudes, technological advances and residential development.

programme.title: Take Me Home
programme.desc: Taxi driver Tom is waved down by Kathy, a lost and distressed young woman who has had a row with her husband. A traumatic first encounter leads to further meetings.

programme.title: Take Me Home
programme.desc: Tom and Kathy have acknowledged a need for each other, and take their affair further. The more carelessly passionate the affair becomes, the greater the danger of discovery.

programme.title: Take Me Home

programme.title: Frozen Planet II
programme.desc: In the far north of the planet lies the largest land habitat on earth, home to snow-covered forests and the icy open tundra. These are lands of extremes that push animals to their limits: in winter they are so cold that much of the ground has remained frozen since the last ice age. To stand any chance of survival, animals must adapt in extreme ways: here a super pack of wolves, 25 strong, has come together to take on the only large prey available to them in winter, American bison.

programme.title: The Great Gatsby
programme.desc: At the centre of the story is Jay Gatsby, whose lust for money and power conceals a deeper passion, his love for Daisy, the woman he met in his early youth but lost to the bullying but wealthy Tom Buchanan. His millions made, Gatsby moves into a mansion close to Daisy, where he holds lavish parties, hoping to win her back.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.sub-title: The Great Gatsby: Midnight in Manhattan
programme.desc: A profile from 2000 of writer F Scott Fitzgerald on the seventy-fifth anniversary of the publication of `The Great Gatsby'. Is it merely 'an entertaining anecdote' or should it be seen as 'the most important novel of the twentieth century'?

programme.title: How the West Was Won
programme.desc: Setting off on a journey to the west in the 1830s, the Prescott family run into a man named Linus, who helps them fight off a pack of thieves. Linus then marries daughter Eve Prescott, and 30 years later goes off to fight in the Civil War with their son, with bloody results. Eve's sister, Lily, heads further west and has adventures with a professional gambler, stretching all the way to San Francisco and into the 1880s.
